answers.answer: Separate Power uses cannot combine Bringer’s hypothetical Damage; 2 plus 1 in separate Powers does not destroy the City. Instructions within one Power can combine, and a Repeat can pretend-destroy the same piece again.

evidence.text:
- **Bringer of Dreams and Nightmares:** Its Powers' explicit Damage/Destroy cannot actually harm Invaders/Dahan or destroy anything except its own Presence. This restriction still applies when that Power's Damage/Destroy instruction names Dahan or another Spirit as the actor. An explicit instruction to Damage or Destroy Dahan does nothing to those Dahan; skip that instruction and resolve the rest of the Power normally. For each Power use, evaluate what it would destroy if resolved normally. Apply these results separately to each would-be-destroyed Invader; the Fear result does not itself grant movement:

  | Would-be-destroyed Invader | Fear | Movement from this special rule |
  | --- | --- | --- |
  | Explorer | 0 | Push it. |
  | Town | 2 | Push it. |
  | City | 5 | No Push. |

  No real Damage is marked, so different Powers or a Repeat cannot combine their hypothetical Damage; multiple instructions **within one Power** can. Existing real Damage from others helps its hypothetical destruction and remains unchanged afterward. Within a single Power use, a given Invader can be pretend-destroyed only once. Repeats can “destroy” the same piece again for Fear. It does not get bonuses conditional on **actual** destruction (e.g., Mists of Oblivion or Vengeance of the Dead) from these pretend destructions. [Core: .7w4g9jv, .7w4g7yx, .7w4g7yu, .7w4g8pj, .9v5kfh3, .9v5katc, .bu6oc6g]

evidence.text:
| Instruction | Effect on the piece |
| --- | --- |
| **Damage** | Mark Damage; reaching Health destroys the piece immediately. |
| **Destroy** | Return the specified piece to supply regardless of Health or marked Damage. |
| **Remove** | Take the specified piece off the board without a Damage-to-Health test. |
| **Replace** | Remove the original piece and put the specified new piece in its place, retaining marked Damage. |

“Damage” means **Damage to Invaders** unless explicitly stated otherwise. Normal Spirit Damage does not harm Dahan or the land. Distribute Damage among Invaders in the target land however you wish; Explorers need not be hit first. Damage from separate normal Powers and counterattacks can accumulate within a turn. [FAQ if-an-invader-with-health-bonus-and-damage-is-moved-where-is-it-destroyed]

**Destroy** returns pieces to supply regardless of Health when directly instructed. Every destroyed Town generates **1 Fear** and every destroyed City **2 Fear**, in addition to explicit Fear from the effect. Explorers generate none automatically. **Remove** returns the specified pieces without requiring Damage to reach their Health and without destruction Fear. Within the effect's count and piece-type restrictions, its decision-maker may choose any eligible pieces; there is no Explorer-first priority unless stated. **Replace** removes a piece and adds another, retaining its marked Damage: the replacement itself produces no Fear, but if the retained Damage destroys the new piece, destruction Fear applies normally. For simultaneous replacements, select all pieces before replacing any: the same original City cannot become a Town and then an Explorer within that one simultaneous instruction. Separate completed instructions or actions may replace the resulting piece again (e.g., successive players resolving **Trade Suffers** at Terror III).
